This hospital is modeled after a hospital for humans in several ways. They have a side entrance for an emergency room, for example. They provide specialist consultations, and in our case during the initial visit an ultrasound was conducted on the spot based on the information we provided.

When you enter the lobby, it is quite large with very high ceilings. Just like you do when you go to say Lusiadas hospital in Porto for yourself, you go to the kiosk, and select your situation and get a number. After they call your number, they will call it again to go to the room on the big board. Very well done.

The layout is that of a hospital and not a clinic. I was not as prepared as I could have been because I was without my dog's passport.

Dra Patricia looked at his records and evaluated our dog. After the Ultrasound, we have a good plan and way ahead. I believe this facility is best if you are in this area, and perhaps if you need to travel further it may still be the better option if time permits.

Good facilities and service.
The service is more expensive, but I understand that's characteristic of emergency care.

Thank you for your feedback.

We are always working to improve.

I'd give them a zero if I could. It was my second visit. The first time was fine, but the second was disastrous. They were more concerned with ripping you off with poor service than with the animal's well-being. But the worst part was paying for a CT scan and then a consultation just to have the results read to me—surreal! But the worst part is that I asked them for the images to consult with another hospital they themselves recommended for the procedure my dog ​​needs, and it turns out they've lost the CT scan images. First, there's a computer problem, and then they claim they deleted the images, when legally they have to keep the images for a certain period of time. Now they're passing the buck. They're absolute crooks. If you value your pets' health, stay away from hospitals like this.
Review updated September 14, 2026. In addition to everything mentioned, their oncologist said that the operation to remove the tumor would require breaking ribs, a four-day hospital stay, and who knows what else. Of course, subjecting a 15-year-old dog to this, even though he's in great shape, we thought it would be a lot of suffering for him. Thankfully, we weren't satisfied with their answer. It turns out that nothing was wrong with the operation; they didn't need to break anything. He was going to stay overnight, but since he wouldn't stay still, it was better for us to take him home. The real shame wasn't that they removed it earlier, because recently, even before the operation, he started producing fluid. And despite having the entire tumor removed, we're now giving him chemotherapy and regularly draining the fluid. So, we also need to investigate this incompetence, which has caused the dog more discomfort and cost me more money.

Thank you for your feedback and trust.

It was a first time, never to be repeated. I've already written everything twice and it was deleted.
It was a terrible experience. He spent a day there without them doing anything except an x-ray. He still hadn't had the stitches in his mouth and without any information about what was happening, and he was left there for the next day. I had to call to get information. Meanwhile, given the quote they gave me, I thought it was excessive to operate on 3 fingers; it would be €800, and then I told them I couldn't afford it.

I asked them to put the stitches in, and the quote was €359.50. They said it would be ready at 5 pm. After an hour of waiting, I asked them to contact me when he was available for discharge. It was 8 pm and nothing. I called several times without success. I went there, and the reception couldn't give me any information, but they already had the amount for me to pay, which turned out to be €371.50. The cost of the medication was still missing.
A nurse came and took me to the room where he was. I told the girl it was unbelievable that he was ready and nobody called, she apologized, saying that normally doctors call. I was really upset but I realized that none of those people were at fault. But honestly, it was total negligence, poor management and organization. I was happy to bring my baby home from there.
